newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's future queen turns 20 as royals thrive.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's future queen turns 20 as royals thrive.

text.p: Sweden's future queen, Victoria, turned 20 on Monday, confident in a country that is happy with its monarchy and showing no signs of British-style royal malaise.
Crown Princess Victoria, who projects a wholesome and attractive public image, will be serenaded by rock group Ace of Base at her birthday party.
But the paparazzi of Sweden have little prospect of snapping the chubby-faced princess getting up to mischief: the royal children of Sweden behave flawlessly in public.

"The children growing up healthy and happy is one thing; the royal family is also untarnished by scandal, the king and queen are admired as people, appear to be an unpretentious normal family and have a relaxed style," said sociologist Ake Daun.
While Britain leads the way in scandalous royalty, followed closely by the Grimaldis of Monaco, Sweden's 1,000-year-old monarchy is going from strength to strength.

Attempts to drag the royal family -- King Carl XVI Gustaf and Queen Silvia have three children -- into the gutter have backfired on Sweden's tabloid media and the press itself has little appetite for downmarket royal stories.

"The problem is that people only want to read happy, positive news on the royal family. They want stories with happy endings," said Tommy Schonstedt, editor of the weekly tabloid magazine Se Och Hor (See And Hear).
The recipe for success with Sweden's royalty appears to be that it is totally devoid of power and plays only a symbolic role in society.
"The less power the king has, the more power he seems to be given," runs a common saying about the head of state.

An opinion poll published last month showed 57 percent of Swedes had "quite a lot" or "very much" confidence in the royal institutions, while the country's political institutions scored just 19 percent.

The king and queen, a smiling couple with just the right dash of idiosyncrasies -- the king was a playboy bachelor, likes sports cars and is a poor public speaker, and the queen is born of a Brazilian mother and a German businessman -- have set the tone for Swedish royalty's popularity.
But the three children -- Carl Philip is 18 and Madeleine 15 -- have put the icing on the cake.

"Crown Princess Victoria celebrated her 20th birthday today in a country where the thousand-year-old monarchy is blooming unfettered," the conservative daily Svenska Dagbladet said in a front-page article.
Victoria spent the last academic year at college in France and begins a political science degree at Uppsale University, north of Stockholm, in September.
